Load WJP Fonts

Source: R/fonts.R
wjp_fonts.Rd

wjp_fonts() loads the fonts used in WJP visualizations. Call it once at the beginning of your R session before creating any WJP chart.

Two engines are available:

  • engine = "showtext" (default) downloads the fonts with sysfonts and activates showtext, which draws text as polygons on any graphics device. This is the historical behavior and works with the base png() and pdf() devices.

  • engine = "systemfonts" makes the static font files available to systemfonts, without showtext. Devices built on systemfonts (ragg, svglite) then write real text that wjp_save() can convert to outlines, and every weight of the fonts can be used.

Usage

wjp_fonts(
  engine = c("showtext", "systemfonts"),
  showtext = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  cache_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

engine

String. "showtext" (default) or "systemfonts".

showtext

Logical. Whether to activate showtext. Defaults to TRUE for the showtext engine and FALSE for the systemfonts engine, which also turns off an active showtext session.

path

String. Optional directory containing the static font files (systemfonts engine only).

cache_dir

String. Directory where downloaded font files are kept (systemfonts engine only). Default is the user cache directory of WJPr.

Value

Invisibly, NULL for the showtext engine, or a data frame with the font files and the families that resolve to them for the systemfonts engine.

Details

Both engines provide the family names used by WJPr:

  • Lato Full: regular (400) and bold (700). Default family of every WJPr chart.

  • Lato Light: light (300) and bold (700).

  • Lato Black: black (900).

  • Inter Tight: regular (400) and bold (700).

The systemfonts engine also makes every static weight of Inter Tight available and registers one family per weight, so that each role of a chart can use its own weight: Inter Tight Medium (500), Inter Tight SemiBold (600), and Inter Tight Bold (700). The text arguments of WJPr charts (e.g., value_fontface) accept the faces "medium", "medium.italic", "semibold", and "semibold.italic", which use these families when they are available and fall back to "bold" and "bold.italic" otherwise (e.g., with the showtext engine or with Lato). WJP country reports print values in Inter Tight SemiBold Italic (value_fontface = "semibold.italic").

Static font files are read from path when supplied (file names as distributed by Google Fonts, e.g. InterTight-SemiBoldItalic.ttf and Lato-Regular.ttf). Otherwise they are downloaded once from Google Fonts into cache_dir. Both fonts are licensed under the SIL Open Font License. Fonts installed on the system with the same family names are superseded by these static files.

WJPr charts use Lato Full by default. To switch every chart and theme to another loaded family (e.g., Inter Tight), set the wjpr.family option once per session: options(wjpr.family = "Inter Tight"). See wjp_font_family().

Examples

# Load fonts before creating charts
wjp_fonts()

# Now you can use the fonts in ggplot2
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, y = wt)) +
  geom_point() +
  theme(text = element_text(family = "Lato Full"))


if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Static files known to systemfonts (text can be outlined on export)
wjp_fonts(engine = "systemfonts")
options(wjpr.family = "Inter Tight")
} # }
